title: The Moon's Shadow Races Across Earth at About 1,500 Miles an Hour

scenes.text: During an eclipse, the Moon's shadow races across Earth at fifteen hundred miles an hour.
That is almost three times faster than a jet airliner.
NASA measured it from space at roughly fifteen hundred to eighteen hundred miles an hour.
It is more than twice the speed of sound.
The shadow is just the Moon blocking sunlight, but it crosses entire countries in hours.
Faster than a jet, and it's only a shadow.

description:
During a total solar eclipse the Moon's shadow sweeps over the ground at about 1,500 miles an hour or more, measured by NASA instruments.
That is more than twice the speed of sound.
Would you chase an eclipse?
first_comment: Would you travel across the world to stand inside that shadow?
